title: Geo processing boundary + KMS review - Stargaze Retail
summary: Redwood team walked through options for EU-only processing, customer-managed KMS, subprocessor list and SOC2/ISO evidence. Customer clarified requirement for no US egress for EU PII, asked about RBAC/SSO, audit logs retention and contract language. Agreed next steps: share SOC2+ISO docs, subprocessor inventory, and schedule technical KMS deep dive and perf bench.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-03-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Sofia Patel, Liam Chen (Redwood); Maya Hernandez, Oliver Grant, Priya Rao (Stargaze)

Summary auto-generated: medium quality transcript - some words unclear (e.g., model names, K V cache spelled variably).

[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood, I've got Liam from our infra team as well. How's your afternoon?
[00:10] Maya (CISO): Good, thanks. We've got about 50 minutes, want to run through our constraints — EU data must stay in EU for certain PII flows, and we need customer-managed keys for those datasets.
[00:22] Liam (SE): Great. Quick preview: we support route-by-region policies, dedicated EU-only pools and private deployments with a VPC control plane. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys — either cloud KMS integrations or HSM with escrow.
[00:35] Oliver (Head of Platform): When you say dedicated EU-only pools, does that mean no cross-border fallbacks? We can't have anything touching US infra for those payloads.
[00:45] Liam (SE): We can pin requests to EU model endpoints; by default we won't route to other regions. There are two caveats: 1) if a customer wants automatic fallback for availability we can enable it, but it would cross borders; 2) some recovery/backup ops in certain scenarios may involve metadata replication — we can exclude sensitive datasets.
[01:05] Maya (CISO): That's the thing — our requirement is strict: no US egress for EU-labeled PII even in failover. Is that captured in the DPA?
[01:12] Sofia (AE): We can add a contractual SLA for region affinity and tie it to processing scope in the DPA. We'll also provide the subprocessor list and flag which subprocessors operate in EU only.
[01:22] Priya (Legal): On subprocessors, we need the complete chain — not just the direct list. Also need to understand data-at-rest encryption with customer KMS; specifically, can Redwood support bring-your-own-key where keys never leave our control?
[01:35] Liam (SE): Yes. We have two patterns: 1) Customer-managed cloud KMS — you provision keys in your cloud project and we call them via IAM. Keys never leave your cloud provider. 2) HSM/Key-escrow — a hardware-backed store we can interoperate with; we can also support KMS proxies in your VPC. There's some subtlety around transient cache encryption — our KV cache may keep tokenized prefixes in GPU memory; we encrypt those with ephemeral keys and your master key wraps them.
[02:08] Oliver (Head of Platform): That KV cache detail — is that encrypted with customer key or Redwood-managed key? We need attestation that nothing is persisted unencrypted outside EU.
[02:18] Liam (SE): The cache is encrypted at rest and in transit. For EU-only configurations we will ensure encryption keys are EU-bound and wrapped with your CMK. There may be a brief window where ephemeral encryption metadata is stored in a control plane but we can configure it to be within EU-only control plane when using Private.
[02:40] Maya (CISO): Ok, also SOC 2/ISO evidence — can you provide your latest reports and a contact for auditors?
[02:47] Sofia (AE): Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs. Note some vendor redactions are applied. I'll include the auditor contact and a summary control matrix.
[02:58] Priya (Legal): Also need to discuss RBAC and SSO — we require SAML SSO and role-based access controls scoped to teams, with audit logging and immutable logs for six years for financial data.
[03:12] Liam (SE): We support SAML and OIDC, and can integrate with your IdP. RBAC supports customizable roles, and we stream audit events to your SIEM over TLS. Immutable retention for six years — we can export to your storage in-region using lifecycle rules; Redwood can also retain but we usually recommend pushing long-term retention to customer-owned buckets.
[03:42] Oliver (Head of Platform): Streaming to our SIEM — what's the schema? We need field names, event types, and a sample.
[03:49] Liam (SE): We'll send a sample event schema. It includes request_id, model, route, user_id (or system actor), region_tag, action, status, and a base64 blob for model output if requested. Small caveat: sometimes field names in earlier exports were a bit different — the export tool changed 'region' to 'zone' once; we'll ensure consistency in the sample.
[04:12] Maya (CISO): Subprocessor inventory — we've seen downstream subprocessors listed without region labels. We need explicit region per subprocessor and data scope per subprocessor.
[04:22] Sofia (AE): We'll provide a CSV with name, country, role (processing/storage), and which dataset types they touch. We'll flag EU-only subprocessors.
[04:30] Priya (Legal): For contractual language, we might need a clause prohibiting cross-border fallback for EU PII and specifying penalties. Is that something Redwood accepts?
[04:39] Sofia (AE): We'll take that to legal — we've done similar amendments for other enterprise customers. We usually accept region affinity clauses tied to a list of dataset tags.
[04:48] Oliver (Head of Platform): Performance question — if we pin to EU-only, any difference in latency or cost?
[04:55] Liam (SE): Minimal latency difference, but cost can vary if EU pool capacity is smaller and we need heavier spec GPUs. Also batching and KV cache locality affects tail latency. We'll provide a perf baseline with EU-only dedicated nodes.
[05:12] Maya (CISO): One more — audit logs immutability. Can you provide SLA/attestation that logs can't be tampered with?
[05:20] Liam (SE): We have write-once storage options and we can sign logs with HSM-backed keys. There's also export-to-customer-storage where immutability is enforced by the customer's storage policies.
[05:34] Priya (Legal): Regarding KMS, does Redwood require key escrowing or do you accept a BYOK model with zero-knowledge on your side?
[05:42] Liam (SE): BYOK is supported; in that model we don't hold the plaintext key. For some managed features we may request a wrapped key; we can provide EKM patterns where operations are authorized by your KMS and Redwood only receives operation tokens.
[06:00] Maya (CISO): What about backups and disaster recovery — where do backups sit? Are snapshots replicated to US?
[06:08] Liam (SE): For EU-only tenants backups can be stored in EU regions only. We can set snapshot replication to EU clouds. If you pick Hosted with EU-only policy we enforce no cross-border replication. For some support scenarios, snapshots may be pushed to our support environment (not containing PII) — we can make that explicit.
[06:30] Sofia (AE): To be clear — we offer three deployment patterns: Hosted (fast onboarding), Dedicated EU-only capacity (reserved GPU pools in EU), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For strict residency, Dedicated or Private is typical.
[06:45] Oliver (Head of Platform): Cost delta between hosted EU-only and dedicated?
[06:50] Liam (SE): Hosted EU-only is usually slightly cheaper, but dedicated gives you stronger isolation and predictable throughput; cost will be tied to reserved GPUs. We'll send a detailed cost comparison.
[07:05] Maya (CISO): Can you describe your incident response for data exfil cases? We need RTO/RPO and notification timelines in the contract.
[07:14] Sofia (AE): We have an incident response policy, 72-hour notification for breaches that affect PII, and runbooks for containment. For customers with strict SLAs we can tighten the notification window as contractually defined.
[07:30] Priya (Legal): We need proof points — have you had any third-party pen tests?
[07:35] Liam (SE): Yes, we commission annual pen tests and will share the engagement summary (redacted).
[07:42] Maya (CISO): Regarding telemetry — does Redwood collect full user prompts for redaction/review? We want to avoid any retention beyond necessary.
[07:51] Liam (SE): By default we log request metadata and limited outputs depending on your setting. You can opt into full prompt retention for evals but for EU PII we'll mark the toggle off and ensure it's not persisted. There have been cases where model debugging required temporary retention; that can be done in a customer-controlled bucket.
[08:15] Oliver (Head of Platform): Network connectivity question — can you peer into our VPC to keep traffic entirely in our network?
[08:21] Liam (SE): For Private deployments yes, VPC peering or PrivateLink style options are available. For Hosted, we offer customer-managed endpoints and white-listed IP ranges but not full peering.
[08:34] Maya (CISO): Audit trail — are all admin actions logged with who/when/where?
[08:40] Liam (SE): Yes, admin actions emit audit events. We include SSO subject, action, timestamp and context. The log retention and export policy can be configured per-tenant.
[08:50] Sofia (AE): Quick check — any competitors in your evaluation list?
[08:53] Oliver (Head of Platform): We're looking at CloudAI and BigModelCorp, and also a smaller infra vendor AtlasEdge.
[08:59] Maya (CISO): We prefer vendors with strong EU presence and documented KMS patterns.
[09:05] Liam (SE): Noted. We'll include references and a short comparator doc.
[09:12] Sofia (AE): Before we wrap — let's make sure we capture next steps.
[09:17] Maya (CISO): Yeah. Also can we get a timeline for getting a pilot up with EU-only routing and CMK? We want to start a pilot in the next 3 weeks.
[09:26] Liam (SE): That's feasible. For a pilot we can stand up a small dedicated EU pool and connect CMK; we typically need two weeks for infra provisioning plus KMS integration work.
[09:36] Priya (Legal): We'll need redlined DPA language; we'll send our markups after you send your baseline.
[09:42] Sofia (AE): Perfect. We'll send the baseline DPA and SOC/ISO docs. Liam will follow up on KMS integration steps and perf bench.
[09:53] Oliver (Head of Platform): One small nit — in a previous export we saw some tool names mis-typed, like 'K V cache' or 'VPC peering' spelled weirdly. Not a blocker but please make your docs consistent.
[10:02] Liam (SE): Appreciate the catch — we'll standardize naming in the technical doc.
[10:08] Maya (CISO): Great. Anything else?
[10:10] Sofia (AE): I think that's it. We'll recap actions and circulate. Thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
